title: Skip-level office hours — prep notes and expected Qs
body:
Goal: quick, personal 30-min drop-in with VP (no slides). I want to be concise, surface 3 wins, 2 blockers, and 1 ask. Keep tone: pragmatic + curious.

Notes to self (topline):
- Intention: signal that platform team is focused on reliability/cost lead work for Q2.
- Quick wins to highlight: 1) 12% reduction in median tail latency for text-gen pipeline after kernel tweak; 2) pilot of new KV cache invalidation reduced repeated cold-cache tokens by ~8%; 3) started Dedicated onboarding for two early-enterprise pilots.
- Blockers to escalate: 1) capacity crunch in eu-west region for Dedicated pilot slot scheduling; 2) delayed infra budget signoff for next-gen autoscaler (impact on sprints 6–8).
- Exact asks: a) unblock budget approval (who to loop: finance lead Helena + CTO sync), b) permission to fast-track two Dedicated pilot GPUs into pool (temp reallocate from internal dev pool).

Opening lines (practice):
- "Thanks for squeezing me in — quick context: I run the platform infra team that owns serving runtime and capacity. Today I want to share 3 quick wins, 2 frictions, and ask for help on one operational decision."

What to surface (metrics & quick evidence):
- Latency: median p50 -> 14ms, p95 -> 68ms, p99 -> 210ms; recent change moved p99 from 260ms -> 210ms (12% drop). Can show a 1-line metric if asked: "dashboard: /ops/latency/serving-runtime".
- Cost: avg per-token GPU compute reduced by ~6% on batch-optimized workloads (note: still early, ran on 10% of traffic).
- Reliability: 99.92% uptime for hosted-api region-us-central last month (one-managed evict event on 02/12).

Anticipated tough questions and suggested responses:
- Q: "Why can't we take capacity from test accounts?"
  A: "We tried that; dev/test pools are on different hardware and can't be easily rehomed due to GPU-driver/OSS kernel divergence. Short-term we can repurpose low-priority dev nodes for 72-hour bursts but it's brittle; recommended path is targeted reallocation from internal burst pool while autoscaler funding completes."

- Q: "Is the latency improvement safe for all customer workloads?"
  A: "We rolled it to 30% of traffic with A/B evals on a breadth of sequence lengths and saw no quality regressions. We do have an open eval for long-seq customers — plan to run 2 weeks more and then flip the rollout to 100%."

- Q: "What does the budget signoff timeline look like?"
  A: "Finance needs a steering memo (1 pager) that shows ROI and criticality. If we can get signoff this week, engineering can start sprint allocation next Monday; otherwise sprint sequencing shifts and the autoscaler work risks slipping 4–6 weeks."

- Q: "Are customers seeing this? Will we need to communicate?"
  A: "Customer-facing impact is currently neutral-to-positive (lower latency/cost). For Dedicated pilots we will send a short heads-up once the extra capacity is confirmed, but no broad customer comms required now."

Possible follow-ups VP might ask me to do during/after call:
- Draft a 1-page ROI memo for finance by EOD Thursday. (Prep: show projected cost reduction, ARR impact assumptions, and risk matrix).
- Connect with Helena (finance) and Maja (head of customer success) so pilots have a soft landing.
- Authorize a temporary reassign of 2 dev GPUs for 72 hrs for one pilot (if VP ok).

Personal prep checklist (what to bring mentally):
- Keep it <30s per win. Avoid deep technical rabbit holes unless VP asks.
- Keep tone: "we're on top of it, but need help on two pragmatic things".
- If asked for details on kernel changes, say: "post-mortem + diff + perf plot in Confluence, happy to sync with eng leads after."

One-paragraph elevator pitch (practice):
- "Platform is focused on three levers: making inference predictable at scale (latency SLOs), making it cost-efficient (batching/quant), and making deployment frictionless (Dedicated/Private onboarding). Small infra changes are stacking into measurable improvements, but the next step (autoscaler / capacity commitment) needs funding to avoid a multi-week schedule slip."

Parking lot (not for call, but to track):
- Investigate longer-term strategy for region capacity forecasting (ML-based forecasting hypothesis: use request pattern clusters + enterprise SLAs).
- Follow-up doc: dedicated pilot runbook (owner: Marta) — include onboarding checklist and data-collection hooks.
- Raise a change to the dev/gpu scheduling policy (ops ticket).

Prep snippets to copy into live chat if needed:
- "TL;DR: 3 wins, 2 frictions, 1 ask — unblock budget + short-term GPU reallocation."
- "If helpful I can drop a 1-pager to finance and copy you — should I loop Helena now?"

Notes to self: breathe, be crisp, lean on numbers not narratives. If conversation turns strategic, offer to schedule a 45-min deep dive with slides next week.

End.
